record.paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
record.original_question: For networking and systems datasets that consist of time series and metadata rather than labeled images, how should GAN fidelity be evaluated when the standard, widely used GAN metrics were designed for image data and cannot be directly applied?

evidence.quote: Evaluating GAN fidelity is notoriously difficult [72, 114]; the most widely-accepted metrics are designed for labelled image data [55, 92] and cannot be applied to our datasets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of evaluating the fidelity of a generative adversarial network (GAN) trained on networked-systems data, where each sample is a pair $(M, X)$ consisting of a metadata vector $M \in \mathcal{M}$ (a mixture of categorical and continuous attributes) and a multivariate time series $X = (x_1, \ldots, x_T) \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times T}$ of variable or fixed length $T$. Let $P_{\text{real}}$ denote the (unknown) joint distribution over $(M, X)$ from which a finite training set is drawn, and let $P_{\text{gen}}$ denote the distribution induced by a trained generator $G$.

The most widely adopted GAN fidelity metrics (such as Inception Score and Fréchet Inception Distance) rely on features extracted by classifiers pretrained on large labeled image corpora and therefore do not apply to $(M, X)$ samples of this form.

Problem. Design a principled, general-purpose methodology for evaluating the fidelity of $P_{\text{gen}}$ relative to $P_{\text{real}}$ in this setting. Specifically:

(a) Propose a quantitative metric, or a finite collection of metrics, $\{\mu_i(P_{\text{real}}, P_{\text{gen}})\}_{i=1}^k$, that
  (i) is well-defined for joint distributions over (metadata, time series) pairs of the form above,
  (ii) captures both marginal statistical properties (e.g., distributions of metadata attributes, marginal value distributions of the time series, autocorrelation structure) and joint properties (e.g., dependence between metadata and temporal dynamics, and long-range temporal correlations),
  (iii) admits consistent finite-sample estimators with quantifiable error,
  (iv) does not depend on a domain-specific pretrained feature extractor.

(b) Provide criteria under which low values of the proposed metrics imply that $P_{\text{gen}}$ is suitable as a substitute for $P_{\text{real}}$ in downstream networked-systems tasks (e.g., classification, anomaly detection, simulation), and conversely identify failure modes that the metrics provably detect.

(c) Compare the proposed metrics, in terms of statistical power and computational cost, against existing alternatives such as classifier two-sample tests, predictive-score gaps (train-on-synthetic / test-on-real), and discrepancies of empirical autocorrelation or attribute distributions.
artifact.status_search_result: No universally accepted fidelity metric exists for GANs over (metadata, time series) data. Recent surveys and benchmarks (ACM Computing Surveys 2023; DeepIntoStreams evaluation pipeline; SeriesGAN 2024) note that GAN evaluation for time series still lags computer vision and relies on ad-hoc combinations of microbenchmarks (marginal/autocorrelation distances, Jensen–Shannon divergence), classifier two-sample tests (e.g., LSTM discriminator), and downstream predictive-score gaps. The problem of a principled, general fidelity metric remains open.

status_evidence.title: Generative Adversarial Networks in Time Series: A Systematic Literature Review
status_evidence.snippet: Metrics to evaluate GANs have been exclusively developed and tested for image data, but models operating on time series data have not been studied at all.
status_evidence.claim: Time-series GAN evaluation metrics remain under-developed compared to image-domain metrics.

status_evidence.title: Evaluation-of-Time-Series-Generative-Models (DeepIntoStreams)
status_evidence.snippet: Pipeline for time series generation with comprehensive evaluation metrics combining marginal, temporal, and downstream-task measures.
status_evidence.claim: Current practice combines multiple heuristic metrics, indicating no single accepted fidelity metric exists.

status_evidence.title: SeriesGAN: Time Series Generation via Adversarial and Autoregressive Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work continues to propose new fidelity criteria for time-series GANs.
status_evidence.claim: Evaluation methodology for time-series GAN fidelity is still an active, unresolved area.
